findings.summary: The 'Only One Can' section lists exclusive features, but ALB-only and NLB-only claims are incomplete and one bullet holds two ideas.
findings.fix: Split into one idea per bullet: 'Only ALB: WAF' and 'Only ALB: path/host rules'.

findings.summary: A bullet packs several ideas (protocols, scale and latency) into one line.
findings.evidence: NLB = Layer 4: TCP, UDP, TLS; millions of req/s, ultra-low latency
findings.fix: Split into 'NLB = Layer 4: TCP, UDP, TLS' and 'NLB: millions of req/s, ultra-low latency'.

findings.summary: The CLI command is shown before the one-line idea; the idea line follows the code instead of preceding it.
findings.evidence: aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes ... Set the delay to 30 seconds
findings.fix: State 'Set the delay to 30 seconds' before the code block.

findings.summary: The 'Healthy app marked unhealthy' mistake is a prose paragraph holding two separate causes.
findings.evidence: A path needing auth or returning 301/302 is not 200. The target security group must also allow the load balancer's security group.
findings.fix: Use two bullets: 'Health path needs auth or redirects (301/302): not 200' and 'Target SG must allow the LB SG'.

findings.summary: Every listener must have a default action, so the 'no default action' case cannot occur and the 503/404 claim is misleading.
findings.evidence: No default action means unmatched requests get 503 or 404.
findings.fix: Say that every listener requires a default action. Unmatched requests go to the default action, and if that is a fixed-response it returns whatever status you configured, such as 404. Advise adding a catch-all default action.

findings.summary: The 'Rule traps' note is a prose pair of sentences holding separate ideas, and the rule-order diagram has no stated conditions.
findings.evidence: Priorities must be unique. No default action means unmatched requests get 503 or 404.
findings.fix: Split into bullets, and label the diagram boxes with example conditions (e.g. /api/*, /img/*).

findings.summary: The create-rule code appears before its one-line idea.
findings.evidence: aws elbv2 create-rule ... /api/* goes to one target group
findings.fix: Put the idea line ahead of the code block.

findings.summary: The table implies launch configurations cannot use Spot, but they support Spot through a maximum price. Only mixed-instances policies require a launch template.
findings.evidence: Mixed instances + Spot | Required | Not supported
findings.fix: Split the row: 'Mixed instances policy (multiple types, On-Demand/Spot mix) | Required | Not supported'. Do not claim launch configurations cannot use Spot.

findings.summary: The ASG bullet list mixes several ideas, and the health-check explanation is split awkwardly across bullets.
findings.evidence: Health check type ELB, not the default EC2 / So instances failing the load balancer check get replaced
findings.fix: Make it one bullet pair: 'Health check type: ELB (default is EC2)' and 'Why: instances failing the LB check get replaced'.

findings.summary: The command block shows four commands with one inline comment, with no idea statement before the code; the update command has no ASG name.
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea before the code and add --auto-scaling-group-name web to the update command.

findings.summary: A policy bullet crams several ideas into one line, and the step example is hard to scan as text rather than a table.
findings.evidence: Step: CloudWatch alarm; CPU 60-70% add 1, above 70% add 3
findings.fix: Split into bullets or a small step table (CPU range / adjustment).

findings.summary: The cheat sheet table omits several chapter facts, and the bullet 'ASG creates and manages the alarms; out fast, in slowly' holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: ASG creates and manages the alarms; out fast, in slowly
findings.fix: Split into two bullets and add target tracking and cross-zone defaults to the cheat sheet rows.

findings.summary: The second question's answer mixes the cause and a fix inside bullets in a way that conflates the failure with the fail-open fallback.
findings.evidence: With all targets unhealthy, the load balancer fails open and routes to all of them.
findings.fix: Label each answer line (Result / Why / Fix) so the outcome is distinct from the fallback behavior.
